title: lint(searchable-fields): the validate-searchable-fields docblock still calls a declared json column "a scan that CAN match"; since #29394 the expansion gives it no clause
body:
domain:spec#3 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbahe4v7GBD94QeSnir

Filing gate: ② an out-of-scope finding the #29546 dev reported on PR #29584 (os-dev-report 6587261679), read by the seat on `origin/main`. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets it.

## What happens

`packages/lint/src/validate-searchable-fields.ts`, the module docblock (~L95-100 on `main`), explains why the object's own `searchableFields` stays existence-only: "a json or lookup column declared THERE is a choice the engine executes (a `$contains` over the stored JSON text / the stored foreign key) — narrow, rarely useful, but a scan that CAN match". Since PR #29502 (#29394) the `$search` expansion (`packages/objectql/src/search-filter.ts`, reading `textOperatorDoorVerdict`) gives a never-string-capable column such as json no clause, so a json entry can never match; a single lookup gets `$icontains`, not `$contains`. #29546 / PR #29584 fixes the same sentence in `packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts`; this is the lint twin.

## Done when

- The docblock says a declared column of a never-string-capable type is admitted but contributes no clause (a set made only of such columns answers no rows), and names the lookup operator the expansion actually uses. Measure both on the tree first.
- Decide, and say in the PR, whether the rationale "neither a 400 nor a finding" still holds for a json entry that can now never match, or whether that is a lint-rule question for a separate card. ⛔ This card changes prose only; no rule behaviour moves.

Comment-only: `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.

Related: #29546 / PR #29584, #29394 / PR #29502.
